t.1.60.1: Then, O tiger among men, the great-souled Viśvāmitra, seeing those sages setting out, spoke to all those forest-dwellers.
t.1.60.2: This great obstacle has arisen and has settled upon the southern quarter. We shall go to another quarter, and there we shall practise austerities.
t.1.60.4: Having spoken thus, the great sage of mighty splendour, subsisting on roots and fruits, performed at Puṣkara fierce and unassailable austerities.
t.1.60.3: In the vast western region, at the Puṣkara lakes of the great-souled one, we shall practise austerities in comfort, for that is the supreme grove of asceticism.
t.1.60.5: At that very time, the king who was lord of Ayodhyā, renowned by the name Ambarīṣa, set about performing a sacrifice.
t.1.60.6: While he was performing the sacrifice, Indra carried off his sacrificial animal. When the animal was lost, the brāhmaṇa said this to the king.
t.1.60.7: O king, the sacrificial animal has today been carried off and is lost because of your misconduct. Faults destroy a king who fails to protect, O lord of men.
t.1.60.8: For this calls for a great expiation, O bull among men; quickly bring back the sacrificial animal, or else a man, while the rite is still in progress.
t.1.60.10: The lord of the earth went searching through those various regions and countries, through cities and forests, and through the holy hermitages.
t.1.60.9: Having heard the words of his preceptor, O best of men, that king of great wisdom searched for a sacrificial animal, offering cows by the thousands in exchange.
t.1.60.11: Dear Raghunandana, he then saw Ṛcīka seated on Bhṛgutunda together with his sons and his wife.
t.1.60.12: The greatly splendid royal sage of boundless radiance, having bowed to and propitiated that brahmin sage Ṛcīka, who blazed with austerity, and having asked after his welfare in every respect, spoke these words to him.
t.1.60.13: If you will sell me your son for a hundred thousand cows, to serve as the sacrificial victim, O illustrious Bhārgava, then I have achieved my purpose.
t.1.60.14: All the lands have been searched, yet I cannot find a sacrificial animal. You ought to give me one son from among these for a price.
t.1.60.15: Thus addressed, the greatly radiant Ṛcīka spoke these words: "O best of men, I would by no means sell my eldest son."
t.1.60.16: Having heard the words of Ṛcīka, the ascetic mother of those great-souled sons spoke to Ambarīṣa, the tiger among men.
t.1.60.17: Know, O king, that to me also the youngest, Śunaka, is dear.
t.1.60.18: For as a rule, O best of men, eldest sons are dear to fathers and the youngest to mothers; therefore I keep the youngest.
t.1.60.20: The father has declared the eldest not to be sold, and the mother the youngest; I consider the middle son to be the one sold, O king, so lead me away.
t.1.60.19: When the sage had spoken his words, and the sage's wife likewise, Śunaḥśepa, the middle son, himself spoke these words, O Rāma.
t.1.60.22: But Ambarīṣa, the royal sage of great splendor and great fame, hastily placed Śunaḥśepa on his chariot and quickly went away.
t.1.60.21: Having acquired Śunaḥśepa for a hundred thousand cows, the lord of men departed, supremely delighted, O Raghunandana.
